findings.claim: fenceRun treats any line starting with three or more backticks or tildes as a fence, whatever follows. Under CommonMark, a backtick fence whose info string contains a backtick is not a fence, e.g. an inline-code line such as ```x``` text. Such a line now opens a fence that never closes, so every later '## ' heading, including '## Log', is swallowed. This is the same invisible-shaper-entry failure the commit set out to fix. Indentation is also unbounded, although CommonMark allows at most 3 spaces.

A fence left unclosed anywhere before '## Log', for example in the Tasks section, now hides the '## Log' heading and every later heading. The parser does not reset the fence state at end of section, and nothing reports the problem. Before the change, such a document parsed correctly. Nothing in the added tests covers an unclosed fence.

evidence: Read the whole diff. The fence state machine only ever changes inside the fenceRun branch, and the '## ' check is gated on fence == "".
The unclosed-fence and inline-code cases are inferred from the code; they are not exercised by the added tests.
